title: The widow's jar (1 Kings 17)
hookLine: a widow shares her last flour with Elijah and it doesn't run out

cards: A prophet walks out of nowhere and tells a king to his face: no dew, no rain, until I say so. His name is Elijah, Elias in the Douay-Rheims, and the king is Ahab, who has turned Israel to the worship of Baal.
The drought comes, and Elijah has to hide. God sends him to a brook, where ravens bring him bread and meat morning and evening. Then the brook dries up.

Then God sends him out of Israel, to Zarephath, a town of Sidon, the homeland of Ahab's queen, Jezebel. I have commanded a widow there to feed you, God says. At the town gate, there she is, picking up sticks.

teach.h: A HANDFUL OF MEAL, A LITTLE OIL.
teach.b: Elijah asks her for a little water. As she goes, he calls after her: and bring me a piece of bread.

She tells him the truth, in the Douay: "I have no bread, but only a handful of meal in a pot, and a little oil in a cruse." She's gathering two sticks to cook it for herself and her son, "that we may eat it, and die."
One last meal, then nothing. Elijah says: Fear not. Go and do it.

teach.h: FIRST MAKE ME A LITTLE CAKE.
teach.b: But first make me a little cake, then make some for yourself and your son.
Because the Lord says the pot of meal will not run out and the jar of oil will not fail until the day the rain comes.
A foreign stranger wants the first bite of her last meal, on the strength of a promise from his God, not hers. And she does it. She went and did according to the word of Elias.
From that day, the meal wasted not, and the oil was not diminished. The text never says the pot filled. It says it never ran out.
Later her son falls ill and stops breathing, and Elijah carries him upstairs, stretches himself over the boy three times, cries to God, and the child lives.
Centuries later, in the synagogue at Nazareth, Jesus reminds his hometown: there were many widows in Israel in Elijah's time, and he was sent to none of them, but to a widow of Sarepta in Sidon.

teach.h: THE POT OF MEAL WASTED NOT.
teach.b: The outsider who shared her last flour.

how: Catholics hear the widow of Zarephath at Mass, paired in one Sunday cycle with the poor widow who gave her two coins in the Gospel of Mark, and parishes often point to her when speaking of giving from need rather than surplus.

s: she lived in Zarephath of Sidon, outside Israel, the homeland of Queen Jezebel.
Elijah asked to be fed first
"first make for me of the same meal a little hearth cake."
the widow's pantry filled up with flour
the pot never filled; it just never ran out, until the rain came.

games.q: you're the widow. you have one handful of flour left for you and your son, and a foreign prophet asks you to bake for him first. what do you do?
o: feed your son first, then share what's left.
bake his cake first, as he asked.
games.why: she does as Elijah says, and the pot of meal wasted not, nor the oil diminished, every day until the rain.

practice: Name what you have least of right now, money, time, patience at the end of the day, and one person who could use a little of exactly that, from the bottom of the pot, not your surplus.
Picture giving it, ten minutes, a meal, a gentle answer, and notice the fear that comes up without arguing. If you pray, hand that fear to God.

wordCard.voice: Zarephath. Where a starving widow fed a stranger first, and her meal and oil never ran out. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: jar, pitcher. The kad of meal that did not run out in Zarephath.

carryVoice: Your line: the jar did not fail. Never full, never empty. That's day four hundred nine.
